thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High error rate detected for hosted inference (us-west2). Symptom: intermittent CUDA illegal memory access / misaligned address in runtime-worker pods. 50% of failures are OOM/container crash related. Starting incident thread. Severity: P1. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/3377778888

alice (oncall): On it — grabbing logs and looking at metrics. First pass: errors started at ~2026-03-15T01:12Z. Any rolling deploys?

ben (sre): Not seeing deploys. I see JVM-level restarts on nodes gpunode-37..40. Kube events show repeated CrashLoopBackOff for runtime-worker-*. Pod logs have `CUDA illegal memory access` + `segfault`.

carla (eng-runtime): Copying relevant stderr from one worker:
```
[2026-03-15 01:12:07] runtime: workers[12] ERROR: CUDA illegal memory access
Backtrace (most recent call first):
  at libtorch::cuda_kernels.cu:0x7ff12ab3
  at runtime::kv_cache::apply_patch(runtime.cc:342)
Signal: SIGSEGV (11)
NVRM: Xid (0000:03:00): 79, GPU page fault on read at address 0x7f12b3c000
```

carla (eng-runtime): Also seeing dmesg on node: `NVRM: GPU at 0000:03:00: Unable to handle kernel page fault at address 0x7f12b3c000` and repeated `invalid device pointer` traces.

devon (platform): I'm going to cordon gpunode-37 and drain it to prevent noisy restarts. Will shift traffic off and let pods reschedule.

alice (oncall): @devon please wait 2m — trying quick hotpatch rollback on the runtime image to the last known-good tag (v3.4.1). If rollback fixes repro we'll keep it.

ben (sre): Observed pattern: failures correlate with long prefix cache hits (KV cache hits) + seq length > 2048. Could be a race in KV cache eviction path.

carla (eng-runtime): Agreed. There's an outstanding kernel-level bug in the custom allocator we landed last month. Reverting allocator to legacy path in image build now. Pushing canary (v3.5.2-canary-alloc-rollback) to a subset of nodes.

incident-bot: Deploy job started: deploy/runtime:v3.5.2-canary-alloc-rollback to runtime-canary-us-west2. CI job: https://ci.redwood.internal/12345

pm-olivia: Customer impact — error rate spike is causing 6% of requests to return 5xx for hosted customers in us-west2. No known data leakage. Notifying account owners for the largest impacted customers.

sre-jordan: Taking oncall handoff in ~25m from alice. If this escalates I’ll be onsite. Any live hotfixes, leave notes here.

alice (oncall): Canary PODs started; initial logs look cleaner. No immediate CUDA faults in canary for 3 minutes. Still seeing faults on older nodes.

ben (sre): Draining gpunode-37 now as devon requested — 4 pods rescheduled to other healthy nodes. GPU metrics: memory pressure was trending up before crash. Could be a leak + pagewalk causing illegal device address once memory recycled incorrectly.

carla (eng-runtime): Rolling the allocator rollback to 30% of fleet. Also adding an extra safety check to KV cache free path to avoid double-free. Will monitor.

alice (oncall): Quick mitigations summary:
- Canary rollback deployed to subset (v3.5.2-canary-alloc-rollback)
- Cordoned gpunode-37, draining in progress
- Autoscaler paused for runtime-workers in us-west2 to avoid noisy scale events
- Alerting thresholds raised to reduce pager noise for correlated OOMs

incident-bot: Metric update: request error rate reduced from 6% -> 1.8% in last 8 minutes after canary. Latency stable.

pm-olivia: Good. Start drafting customer communication: "We experienced elevated 5xx errors in us-west2 due to GPU runtime crashes; mitigation in progress; no data exposure." I'll post once we confirm stable for 30m.

ben (sre): Still seeing a smattering of crashes on node gpunode-39. Collecting `kubelet` + `dmesg` and dumping coredumps for the container. Command run:
```bash
kubectl logs runtime-worker-abc -n runtime --previous
scp root@gpunode-39:/var/crash/core.runtime-worker-abc /tmp/
strings /tmp/core.runtime-worker-abc | grep -i cuda || true
```
Found kernel OOPS entries referencing `smmu` and `pagewalk`.

carla (eng-runtime): I'm building a hotfix with defensive guards and adding a runtime flag to disable the new allocator at runtime. Planning to push with immediate restart for runtime-workers in us-west2 if canary remains healthy.

alice (oncall): @sre-jordan handing off in 20. Leaving checklist in the runbook:
- Confirm canary stable for 30m
- Uncordon nodes if healthy, otherwise reprovision
- Keep autoscaler paused until next deploy
- Upload coredumps + attach to incident ticket

sre-jordan: Thanks — I'll monitor overnight. If we see >2% error rate we'll escalate and perform full fleet rollback to v3.4.1.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Timeline added to incident ticket.

alice (oncall): Final note: root cause suspected to be a race in KV cache eviction interacting with the new allocator and certain long-sequence pathological requests that exercise large KV lifetimes. Follow-up: eng-runtime to run a regression test harness with long prefix sequences and heavy concurrent eviction.

carla (eng-runtime): Will own the postmortem and put the regression test into CI. Initial blamestack points to allocator change set 0x9f3c.

pm-olivia: I'll coordinate customer comms and include mitigation timeline.

ben (sre): Dumped cores uploaded to https://artifacts.redwood.internal/incidents/3377778888/cores.tar.gz

sre-jordan: I'm now primary. Leaving watch on the alerts dashboard. If anything changes ping @sre-jordan and @carla.

incident-bot: Ticket updated. Incident marked "resolved->monitoring" at 2026-03-15T01:45Z.

alice (oncall): Closing my shift. Good job team — will sync in the postmortem. :thumbsup:
